chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from al-Hasan ibn Abdillah, who said:

Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays and Ibn Abi Ya'fur traveled together. One of them ate the slaughtered meat of the Jew and the Christian, while the other refused to eat it. They met at the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him. He asked, 'Which of you refused?' He said, 'I.' He said, 'Well done.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the slaughtered meat of Jews and Christians according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani highlights the juristic nuance in the school of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the meat of the People of the Book, where the Imam’s praise for the companion who abstained suggests a preference for caution (ihtiyat) rather than a strict prohibition. It reflects the historical scholarly debate between those who consider their slaughter valid based on Quran 5:5 and those who emphasize the specific conditions of the slaughterer's piety. The incident underscores the practical application of fiqh principles in daily life during the early Shia community.
